s: Which one of the following is the correct expansion of UMANG?
o: Universal Mobile Application for National Governance
Universal Mechanism for Administrative and New Governance
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
Unified Management Application for New Government
x: UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.

s: Which single application gives access to Central and State Government services such as tax, EPF, gas and passport services through web, SMS and IVR?
x: UMANG offers multiple Central and State services through web, SMS and IVR.

s: Participative governance is most directly associated with which platform?
x: MyGov is a citizen-engagement platform intended to promote participative governance.

s: In which years were Aadhaar launched and the Aadhaar Act enacted, respectively?
x: Aadhaar was launched in 2009; the Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016 and amended in 2019.

s: When was the UMANG app launched?
x: UMANG was launched in November 2017; it was integrated with DigiLocker in October 2024.

s: Which single emergency number is linked to the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS)?
x: ERSS uses the single emergency number 112.

s: What is the name of the Government of India's cloud initiative that hosts government applications?
x: GI Cloud is named MeghRaj; it hosts government applications.

s: When was the BHIM app, based on UPI, launched?
x: BHIM, the UPI app of NPCI, was launched on 30 December 2016.

s: What is the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), launched in 2016 by the Commerce Ministry?
o: A one-stop online public procurement portal
x: GeM (2016, Commerce Ministry) is a one-stop online portal for public procurement.

s: Where were the first Aadhaar numbers issued on 29 September 2010?
x: The first Aadhaar numbers were issued at Tembhli in Maharashtra on 29 September 2010.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Platform)
A. DigiLocker
B. MyGov
C. ERSS
D. CSC
List-II (Purpose)
1. Citizen engagement
2. Cloud locker for documents
3. Village-level service outlets
4. Single emergency number 112
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: DigiLocker stores documents, MyGov is for participation, ERSS uses 112 and CSCs are village service outlets.

s: In October 2024, DigiLocker was integrated with which platform?
x: In October 2024 DigiLocker was integrated with UMANG so stored documents can be used in UMANG services.

s: Which organisation developed the Unified Payments Interface (UPI)?
x: UPI is run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI); the BHIM app works on it.

s: How many services did the UMANG app offer at its launch in November 2017?
x: At launch UMANG offered 162 services from 33 departments and 4 states.

s: How many users did DigiLocker have as of August 2026?
x: DigiLocker had 72.43 crore users in August 2026.

s: Which year was declared the 'Technology-Driven Decision Making Year' in Andhra Pradesh by CM Naidu?
x: CM Naidu declared 2026 the Technology-Driven Decision Making Year in AP.

s: With which of the following is the objective of e-Pragati associated?
o: A unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture
A network limited to district treasuries
x: e-Pragati is a unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture. It aims at faceless, paperless and cashless governance.

s: In which year was Andhra Pradesh's Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) established?
x: RTGS, AP's flagship digital-governance platform using a Data Lake and real-time dashboards, was set up in 2017.

s: The primary purpose of e-Procurement in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Register births and deaths through village offices
Conduct online tendering and help stop collusion
Monitor consumer grievances at the national level
x: The e-Procurement initiative, introduced in 2003, enabled online tendering with the objective of stopping collusion.

s: In which year was MeeSeva, meaning 'At your service', introduced in Andhra Pradesh?
x: MeeSeva was introduced in 2011 as a single-window G2C service centre initiative.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
x: A is correct: eSeva (2001) set up integrated citizen service centres for bills and certificates. B is wrong: MeeSeva came in 2011 as single-window G2C centres, while online tendering was e-Procurement (2003). C and D pair the initiatives with wrong years and purposes.

s: With which organisation was Andhra Pradesh's Prajavani grievance portal for District Collectorates built?
x: Prajavani is a web portal for grievances at district collectorates built with NIC.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Prajavani is an improved version of which Uttar Pradesh e-governance project?
x: Prajavani was modelled as an improved version of UP's Lokvani grievance system.

s: What is the purpose of CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department), launched in Andhra Pradesh in 1998?
o: Computerised registration of land and property deeds
x: CARD (1998) computerised the registration of land and property deeds; its newer version is CARD-PRIMME.

s: What is APSWAN in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A data network linking the Secretariat with district and mandal offices
A chain of citizen service centres
x: APSWAN, the AP State Wide Area Network, is the data backbone linking the Secretariat, district and mandal offices.

s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh e-governance initiatives in chronological order:
1. MeeSeva
2. eSeva
3. CARD
4. Real Time Governance Society
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: CARD (1998), eSeva (2001), MeeSeva (2011) and RTGS (2017).

s: Which was Andhra Pradesh's pioneering integrated citizen service centre, launched in 2001?
x: eSeva (2001) was AP's pioneering integrated citizen service centre for bills and certificates.

s: When was the Meekosam grievance platform launched statewide in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Meekosam had a soft launch in February 2015 and went statewide on 26 May 2015.

s: What is the name of the newer version of Andhra Pradesh's CARD registration system, introduced in September 2023?
x: CARD (1998) computerised property registration; its newer version CARD-PRIMME came in September 2023.

s: In which districts was the Meekosam grievance platform soft-launched in February 2015?
x: Meekosam was soft-launched in Krishna and Anantapuram districts in February 2015 and went statewide on 26 May 2015.

s: Which AI-based grievance system followed Spandana in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The sequence in AP was Prajavani, Meekosam, Spandana and then the AI-based Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS).

s: Which of the following is associated with Andhra Pradesh's Real Time Governance Society (RTGS)?
o: A Data Lake and a Command and Control Centre
x: RTGS (2017) uses AI, Big Data, GIS and IoT with real-time dashboards, a Data Lake and a Command and Control Centre.

s: What was the main aim of the Jawahar Knowledge Centres (JKC) in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Online receipt of grievances at District Collectorates
Training college students in technical and soft skills to make them employable
x: JKCs were an AP government human-resource initiative that trained students in technical, soft and project skills.

s: The Institute for Electronic Governance, which runs the Jawahar Knowledge Centres, is a society under which Andhra Pradesh department?
x: The JKC programme is run by the Institute for Electronic Governance (IEG), a society under AP's IT&C Department.

s: In which year were the National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG) started?
x: NAeG, instituted by DARPG, began in 2003 and are presented at the National Conference on e-Governance.

s: What did the Jaipur Declaration of the 29th National Conference on e-Governance mainly deal with?
o: DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance
Extension of NeSDA to low-connectivity areas
Launch of the National e-Governance Plan
x: The 29th NCeG in Jaipur adopted the Jaipur Declaration on DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance. NeSDA extension was in the Visakhapatnam Declaration.

s: The Visakhapatnam Declaration of the 28th National Conference on e-Governance called for extending which framework to low-connectivity areas?
x: The Visakhapatnam Declaration (2025) sought to extend the NeSDA framework to low-connectivity areas such as Ladakh and the North-East.

s: For which of the following did the 2025 National Awards for e-Governance introduce a dedicated category for the first time?
x: The 2025 awards, conducted with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, introduced a first-ever dedicated category for Gram Panchayats.

s: Who institutes the National Awards for e-Governance?
x: NAeG is instituted by DARPG under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

s: Where was the 28th National Conference on e-Governance held in 2025?
x: The 28th NCeG (2025) was held at Visakhapatnam and adopted the Visakhapatnam Declaration.

s: In which city was the 29th National Conference on e-Governance held in 2026?
x: The 29th NCeG (2026) was held at Jaipur and adopted the Jaipur Declaration.

s: Which Gram Panchayat won the Gold award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026?
x: At NAeG 2026, Rohini Gram Panchayat in Dhule, Maharashtra, won Gold.

s: For which project did Andhra Pradesh's Civil Supplies Department win a Gold award at the 20th National Conference on e-Governance (2017)?
x: At the 20th NCeG (Visakhapatnam, January 2017) AP won Gold for the Aadhaar-enabled PDS in citizen-centric service delivery.

s: Where was the 20th National Conference on e-Governance held in January 2017?
x: The 20th NCeG was held at Visakhapatnam on 9-10 January 2017; AP won Gold awards there.

s: To which of the following does BharatNet aim to provide optical fibre broadband?
x: BharatNet takes optical fibre broadband to Gram Panchayats.

s: What does PM-WANI, launched in December 2020, provide?
x: PM-WANI (Department of Telecom) sets up public Wi-Fi hotspots; PMGDISHA handles rural digital literacy.

s: Which scheme addresses the skills gap of the digital divide through rural digital literacy?
x: PMGDISHA is the rural digital literacy scheme; BharatNet closes the infrastructure gap and PM-WANI the access gap.

s: As of March 2026, about how many Gram Panchayats had been connected under BharatNet?
x: BharatNet had connected 2.15 lakh Gram Panchayats by March 2026; 2.64 lakh is the Amended BharatNet target.

s: How many Gram Panchayats does the Amended BharatNet Programme (August 2023) aim to connect in ring topology?
x: The Amended BharatNet Programme of August 2023 targets 2.64 lakh Gram Panchayats in ring topology.

s: Which department implements PM-WANI, the public Wi-Fi hotspot scheme launched in December 2020?
x: PM-WANI provides public Wi-Fi hotspots through the Department of Telecommunications.

s: How many individuals had been trained in digital literacy under PMGDISHA by 31 March 2024?
x: PMGDISHA, the rural digital literacy scheme, had trained 6.39 crore individuals by 31 March 2024.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a significance of e-governance?
x: E-governance is associated with citizen engagement, better service delivery, fewer face-to-face contacts and audit trails. It does not remove audit trails; digital systems can strengthen them.

s: How is the aim of e-governance often summed up?
x: E-governance uses ICT to deliver services with the aim of faceless, paperless, cashless governance.

s: What is the effect of e-governance on audit trails?
o: It replaces them with manual registers
x: Every digital transaction leaves a record, so e-governance strengthens audit trails rather than removing them.

s: Who is associated with the five models of e-governance comprising broadcasting, critical flow, comparative analysis, e-advocacy and interactive service?
x: The five models listed are attributed to Arie Halachmi.

s: Information on corruption is channelled electronically to an ombudsman. This illustrates which model of e-governance?
x: Critical flow channels critical information to a targeted audience, such as corruption data sent to an ombudsman.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Halachmi's model of e-governance is wrongly matched?
o: Comparative analysis – Learning from best practices elsewhere
E-advocacy – Online civil-society networks influencing decisions
E-advocacy – Learning from best practices elsewhere
Interactive service – Two-way G2C services such as filing, payments and feedback
x: Learning from best practices is comparative analysis; e-advocacy means online civil-society networks influencing decisions.

s: A citizen applies online for an income certificate through UMANG or MeeSeva. Which type of e-governance interaction is this?
x: G2C means Government to Citizen interaction. Online birth, income and caste certificates are examples of G2C services.

s: Which of the following is an example of G2B interaction?
o: GSTN and e-Procurement services for businesses
Online HR tools for government employees
Online birth certificate services for citizens
x: G2B means Government to Business interaction; MCA portal, GSTN and e-Procurement are examples.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of e-governance interaction?
o: G2G refers to interaction between departments or governments
G2E refers to interaction between different governments
NIC solutions, SWAN and e-Office are G2G examples
Online HR and administrative tools are G2E examples
x: G2E means services from government to its employees; interaction between governments is G2G.

s: NIC solutions, SWAN and e-Office are examples of which type of e-governance interaction?
x: NIC, SWAN and e-Office link departments and governments, so they are G2G.

s: When was the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) approved by the Government?
x: NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006; e-Kranti was approved on 25 March 2015 and Digital India launched on 1 July 2015.

s: How many Mission Mode Projects did the NeGP have when approved in 2006?
x: NeGP began with 27 MMPs; 4 added in 2011 made 31, and e-Kranti raised it to 44.

s: What is the vision of e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)?
x: e-Kranti's vision statement is 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.

s: Under e-Kranti, the 44 Mission Mode Projects are split into how many Central, State and Integrated MMPs respectively?
x: e-Kranti has 15 Central, 17 State and 12 Integrated MMPs, totalling 44.

s: Which four Mission Mode Projects were added to NeGP in 2011?
x: In 2011 Health, Education, PDS and Posts were added, taking NeGP to 31 MMPs.

s: When did the Union Cabinet approve e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)?
x: e-Kranti, the second phase of NeGP, was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 March 2015.

s:
Consider the following statements about e-Kranti:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2015.
2. It is one of the pillars of the Digital India programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) was approved on 25 March 2015 and is a pillar of Digital India.

s: Which of the following was NOT part of the core infrastructure of the National e-Governance Plan?
x: NeGP's core infrastructure was SWAN, State Data Centres and CSCs; UMANG came only in 2017.

s: When was the Digital India programme launched?
x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015; 25 March 2015 is the e-Kranti approval date.

s: Which is the implementing ministry of the Digital India programme?
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
x: Digital India is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine pillars of Digital India?
x: A satellite launch programme is not a Digital India pillar; e-Kranti, Early Harvest Programmes and IT for Jobs are.

s: How many pillars does the Digital India programme have?
x: Digital India rests on nine pillars, from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest Programmes.

s: Which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 gives legal recognition to electronic records?
x: Section 4 recognises electronic records; Section 5 recognises digital signatures.

s: Retention of electronic records is provided for under which section of the IT Act, 2000?
x: Section 7 lets a legal duty to retain records be met in electronic form.

s: Which pair relating to the IT Act, 2000 is wrongly matched?
o: Section 4 – Legal recognition of electronic records
Section 5 – Legal recognition of digital signatures
Section 6 – Use of electronic records in Government
x: Retention of electronic records is Section 7; Section 9 says there is no right to insist on electronic acceptance.

s: Which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 gives legal recognition to digital signatures?
x: Section 5 treats electronic (digital) signatures like handwritten ones; Section 4 covers electronic records.

s: Which section of the IT Act, 2000 says that no one can insist that a government document be accepted in electronic form?
x: Section 9 says Sections 6 to 8 give no right to insist on acceptance of a document in electronic form.

s: Which State passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory?
x: Meghalaya passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory in 2017.

s: Which State pioneered State-wide social audits of MGNREGA works?
x: Andhra Pradesh pioneered State-wide MGNREGA social audits; Meghalaya passed the first social audit law in 2017.

s: The Second ARC recommended that social audits be:
o: Institutionalised in all major welfare schemes
x: The Second ARC recommended institutionalising social audits in all major welfare schemes, beyond MGNREGA alone.

s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, 2005, who conducts the social audit of all works?
x: Section 17 makes the Gram Sabha audit all works; social audit is MGNREGA's accountability tool, not a CVC function.

s: In which year was the AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency (SSAAT) set up?
x: SSAAT, an independent society, was set up in 2009; 2005 is the year of MGNREGA. AP pioneered state-wide MGNREGA social audits.

s: Which one of the following Andhra Pradesh initiatives provided web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates?
x: Prajavani was an earlier Andhra Pradesh initiative for online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates.

s: What is Meekosam in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Single-window portal to lodge grievances and suggestions and track their status
Portal for social audits of MGNREGA works
x: Meekosam let citizens lodge grievances and suggestions through a single window and track their status.

s: During which party's government was Spandana launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2019?
x: Spandana was associated with the YSRCP Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh grievance platform was launched in 2015 under the TDP government?
x: Meekosam ('For You') was launched in 2015 under the TDP government; Spandana came in 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about the ombudsman in India:
1. The institution of ombudsman originated in Sweden in 1809.
2. The term 'Lokayukta' was coined by Morarji Desai.
3. Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: Sweden, 1809. Statement 2 is wrong: L.M. Singhvi coined the term; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC that recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta. Statement 3 is correct: Maharashtra, 1971. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include the false statement 2, D includes all.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the First Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Morarji Desai was associated with it
It recommended a Lokpal in each State and Lokayuktas at the Union level
It recommended a Lokpal at the Union level
x: It recommended a Lokpal for the Union and Lokayuktas for the States, not the other way round.

s: Which State set up India's first Lokayukta in 1971?
x: Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.

s: Who coined the terms 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta'?
x: L.M. Singhvi coined the terms in the Lok Sabha in 1963; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC.

s: In which country did the Citizens' Charter originate in 1991?
x: The Citizens' Charter began in the UK in 1991 under the John Major government; India adopted it in 1997.

s: Under which Prime Minister of the United Kingdom was the Citizens' Charter launched in 1991?
x: The Citizens' Charter was launched in 1991 by the John Major government.

s: What happened to the Citizens Charter Bill, 2011, on time-bound delivery of services and grievance redress?
o: It lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 2014
It was withdrawn by the Government in 2012
x: The Bill never became law; it lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2014.

s: Which of the following is one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; participation is not one.

s: What is a Citizens' Charter?
o: Constitutional guarantee enforceable in every court
Statutory code that penalises every service delay
Written commitment on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress
x: A Citizens' Charter records commitments on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress; it is not by itself legally enforceable.

s: In which year did India adopt the Citizens' Charter?
x: India adopted it in 1997; 1991 is its UK origin. DARPG coordinates the charters (goicharters.nic.in).

s: Which body recommended statutory status for Citizens' Charters in India?
x: The Second ARC recommended statutory status for Citizens' Charters, which at present are non-justiciable.

s: What is the legal nature of Citizens' Charters in India?
x: Citizens' Charters are non-justiciable; the 2011 Bill never became law.

s: Which of the following is NOT a basic element of a Citizens' Charter in India?
o: A legally enforceable right to compensation
x: Charters set standards, inform citizens and provide grievance redress, but they are non-justiciable and give no enforceable right.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; participation is not one.

s: Which department coordinates the formulation of Citizens' Charters in the Government of India?
x: DARPG coordinates Citizens' Charters, with nodal officers in every ministry and the website goicharters.nic.in.

s: Which grievance mechanism is an independent officer of the legislature?
x: The classic Ombudsman is an independent officer of the legislature dealing with maladministration; CPGRAMS handles service-delivery grievances and Lokpal handles corruption.

s: With which of the following do the Lokpal and Lokayukta mainly deal?
x: Lokpal and Lokayukta deal with corruption allegations; the classic ombudsman deals with maladministration.

s: In which year was the Act that gives statutory basis to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas passed?
x: Lokpal and Lokayukta are statutory bodies under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013.

s: What does the classic ombudsman mainly deal with?
x: The classic ombudsman, an independent officer of the legislature, deals with maladministration.

s: Which State enacted India's first Right to Services law?
x: Madhya Pradesh's Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010 was the first; Bihar followed in 2011.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The concept of Right to Services grew out of the Citizens' Charter idea in Great Britain.
2. Bihar enacted India's first Right to Services law in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The RTS idea came from Britain; the first law was Madhya Pradesh's in 2010, and Bihar followed in 2011.

s: Which State followed Madhya Pradesh by enacting a Right to Services law in 2011?
x: Madhya Pradesh enacted the first RTS law in 2010; Bihar followed in 2011.

s: Among the following States, which enacted its Right to Services law earliest?
x: The order of enactment among these is Punjab, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

s: Which of the following is NOT a normal feature of Right to Services legislation?
o: Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms
A penalty on the responsible official
A right of appeal in case of delay
Notification of services to be delivered within a fixed time
x: Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials. They do not automatically abolish all other grievance mechanisms.

s: From which date did Andhra Pradesh's Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act come into force?
x: The AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 is in force from 18 October 2017.

s: Which law provides time-bound delivery of notified services in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017
AP Right to Public Services Act, 2011
x: The AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 (Act 6 of 2018) gives time-bound delivery with appeal and penalty.

s: The word “Sevottam” is formed from which combination?
x: Sevottam is derived from “Seva” and “Uttam”, conveying excellence in service.

s: Under Sevottam, which module is correctly matched with its focus?
o: Public Grievance Redress – Publish service standards
x: The Citizens' Charter module publishes service standards; Grievance Redress handles complaints and Service Delivery Capability builds organisational capacity.

s: Sevottam-compliant certification follows which standard?
x: Sevottam-compliant certification follows Indian Standard IS 15700:2005.

s: In which year did implementation of the Sevottam model in government departments begin?
x: Sevottam, suggested in the Second ARC's 12th Report and promoted by DARPG, was implemented from 2009; 2005 is when the Second ARC was set up.

s: How many modules does the Sevottam model have?
x: Sevottam has three modules: Citizens' Charter, Public Grievance Redress and Service Delivery Capability.

s: Which body promotes the Sevottam model in India?
x: DARPG promotes Sevottam, which the Second ARC's 12th Report suggested.

s: What is the title of the Second ARC's 12th Report (2009)?
o: Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Promoting e-Governance – The Smart Way Forward
x: The 12th Report (2009) is 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance'; the 4th Report is 'Ethics in Governance'.

s: Who chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, set up in 2005?
x: Veerappa Moily chaired the Second ARC; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Second ARC's 12th Report:
1. It suggested the Sevottam model.
2. It recommended statutory backing for Citizens' Charters.
3. It wanted social audits confined to MGNREGA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; it wanted social audits institutionalised in all major welfare schemes beyond MGNREGA.

s:
Consider the following statements about CPGRAMS:
1. It was launched in 2007 by DARPG.
2. DARPG functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. It is accessible 24x7 through the web, an app and UMANG.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: CPGRAMS was launched in 2007 by DARPG. Statement 2 is wrong: DARPG is under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions. Statement 3 is correct: 24x7 via web, app and UMANG. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include the false statement 2, D includes all.

s: A circular of DARPG dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time for CPGRAMS grievances from:
x: The DARPG circular dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time from 30 days to 21 days.

s: Which of the following is a dimension of the Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index (GRAI)?
x: GRAI's four dimensions are efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment; transparency is not one.

s: What is the full form of CPGRAMS, the online grievance platform run by DARPG?
o: Central Public Grievance Registration and Management System
Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
Citizen Public Grievance Resolution and Monitoring Scheme
Centralised Pension and Grievance Redress Monitoring System
x: B is the correct expansion: Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System, launched in 2007 by DARPG. A, C and D are invented expansions; D also mixes in pensions, which have a separate platform, CPENGRAMS.

s: What is the name of the separate platform that handles pensioners' grievances?
x: Pensioners use CPENGRAMS, separate from CPGRAMS.

s: In which year was CPGRAMS launched?
x: CPGRAMS was launched in 2007 by DARPG.

s: How many indicators does the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) use?
x: GRAI uses 11 indicators grouped in 4 dimensions: efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment.

s: In which year was Sweden's Freedom of the Press Act, regarded as the world's first freedom-of-information law, enacted?
x: Sweden's 1766 Freedom of the Press Act was the first such law; UDHR Article 19 (1948) later recognised the right to seek information.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS):
1. It held public hearings (jan sunwais) in Rajasthan demanding access to muster rolls and bills.
2. It was led by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Medha Patkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the MKSS jan sunwais on muster rolls and bills in Rajasthan started the RTI movement. Statement 2 is wrong: the MKSS leaders were Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh, not Medha Patkar. So A; B picks only the wrong statement, C accepts it, D rejects the correct statement 1.

s: Which document of 1948 recognised the right to seek and receive information as a human right?
x: Article 19 of the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) recognised the right to seek and receive information.

s: Which was the first Indian State to enact a Right to Information law (1997)?
x: Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997. Sweden had the world's first RTI law (1766), and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.

s: Who founded the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan, whose jan sunwais started the RTI movement?
o: Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt
Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh
x: MKSS (1990) was founded by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh, not Medha Patkar.

s: Which Act of 2002 was never notified and was later repealed by the Right to Information Act, 2005?
x: The Freedom of Information Act, 2002 was never notified and was repealed by the RTI Act, 2005.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Freedom of Information Act in India
2. Freedom of the Press Act of Sweden
3. Right to Information Act in India
4. Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Sweden 1766, UDHR 1948, FOI Act 2002 and RTI Act 2005.

s: On which dates did the Right to Information Act, 2005 receive Presidential assent and come fully into force, respectively?
x: B is correct: assent was given on 15 June 2005 and the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005. A gives the Rajya Sabha passage date as assent; C gives the Lok Sabha passage date as assent; D gives a wrong commencement date.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Passage of the RTI Bill by the Lok Sabha
B. Passage of the RTI Bill by the Rajya Sabha
C. Presidential assent to the RTI Act
D. Full commencement of the RTI Act
Select the correct sequence.
x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 May 2005, the Rajya Sabha on 12 May 2005, assent was given on 15 June 2005, and the Act fully came into force on 12 October 2005.

s: Who was the first Chief Information Commissioner of India?
x: The CIC was constituted on 12 October 2005 with Wajahat Habibullah as the first Chief Information Commissioner. Vajja Srinivasa Rao is the AP State Chief IC.

s: The RTI Act came fully into force how many days after Presidential assent?
x: Assent was given on 15 June 2005 and the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005, after 120 days.

s: When was the Central Information Commission constituted?
x: The CIC was constituted on 12 October 2005, when the RTI Act came fully into force.

s: Which President gave assent to the Right to Information Act, 2005?
x: President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam gave assent on 15 June 2005.

s: Which law gives the citizens of India a statutory right to seek information from public authorities?
x: The RTI Act, 2005 gives every citizen a statutory right to information and mandates a timely reply.

s: The right to know has been judicially read into which Article of the Constitution?
x: Courts have read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a), and also Article 21, in cases like State of U.P. v. Raj Narain and S.P. Gupta.

s: With which of the following does the Preamble of the RTI Act mainly link an informed citizenry and transparency?
o: Containing corruption and holding governments accountable
Making every document public without exception
x: The Preamble ties informed citizenship and transparency to containing corruption and ensuring accountability, harmonised with other public interests.

s: What is the nature of the right created by the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Fundamental Right under a separate Article
Constitutional right of public officials only
x: The Act creates a statutory right; separately, the Supreme Court has read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. It aims at an informed citizenry and transparency to contain corruption and hold governments accountable.
2. It seeks to harmonise transparency with the need to keep some information confidential.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Preamble links transparency with containing corruption and accountability, and harmonises it with confidentiality needs.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution?
o: State of U.P. v. Raj Narain
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
x: In State of U.P. v. Raj Narain the right to know was read into Article 19(1)(a).

s: Frivolous or bulk requests by applicants and bad-faith use of Section 8 by authorities show that the RTI Act has been misused by whom?
x: Applicants misuse it through frivolous or bulk requests, and authorities through delays and bad-faith use of Section 8, so misuse is by both.

s: Under the Right to Information framework, information is provided free of cost to applicants belonging to which category?
o: All applicants below 25 years of age
All applicants belonging to rural areas
x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.

s: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, which of the following is included within the meaning of ‘information’?
o: Information personally generated by an applicant after filing a request
Only physical records maintained by public authorities
Material in any form, including records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data
Only final judicial decisions published in the Gazette
x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.

s: What does Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005 deal with?
o: Constitution of the State Information Commission
x: Section 11 covers third-party information; Section 19 covers appeals and Section 15 the SIC.

s: Which of the following RTI Act provisions is correctly matched?
o: Section 18 – Complaints and inquiry by the Commission
x: Section 18 deals with complaints and inquiry by the Commission. Section 2(h) defines public authority, Section 4 proactive disclosure and Section 19 appeals.

s: Which bodies are public authorities under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act?
o: Only bodies created directly by the Constitution
Only bodies established by an Act of Parliament
Bodies set up by law or government notification, and bodies substantially financed or controlled by government
x: Section 2(h) covers bodies set up by law or notification and those substantially financed or controlled by government, not just constitutional bodies.

s: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, an applicant seeking information:
o: Must state the reasons for seeking it
Need not give any reason for seeking it
x: No reasons are needed; applications may be made by post, in person or by e-mail, in Hindi, English or the local official language.

s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 provides for the constitution of the Central Information Commission?
x: Section 12 constitutes the CIC; Section 15 the SIC, Section 5 covers PIOs and Section 9 copyright-based rejection.

s: On which matters must organisations excluded under Section 24 of the RTI Act still disclose information?
x: Section 24 generally excludes listed intelligence and security organisations, but information on corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ‘right to information’ under Section 2(j)?
o: Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion
Taking notes, extracts or certified copies
Inspection of works, documents and records
x: Section 2(j) includes inspection, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information. It does not require an authority to create a new explanation or opinion.

s: To which provision did the violations found in the Andhra Pradesh Information Commission's statewide inspection mainly relate?
o: Section 7 and payment of RTI fees
x: The inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b), which concerns proactive or suo motu disclosure of information.

s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 gives it overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923?
x: Section 22 makes the RTI Act override the Official Secrets Act, 1923.

s: Which of the following pairs (RTI Act Section – subject) is correctly matched?
x: Section 25 provides for the annual report; 18 is complaints, 19 appeals and 20 penalties.

s: Under the RTI Act, who designates Public Information Officers?
x: Under Section 5, each public authority designates its PIOs and APIOs.

s: In which languages can a request for information be made under Section 6 of the RTI Act?
o: Hindi, English or the official language of the area
x: A request can be made in Hindi, English or the local official language, by post, in person or by e-mail.

s: Under Section 3 of the RTI Act, who has the right to information?
o: All persons living in India, including foreigners
x: Section 3 gives the right to every citizen; only citizens can apply.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Section 24 exempt organisation under the RTI Act, 2005, being the appellate information body?
x: The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation. The IB, R&AW and CRPF are covered by Section 24.

s: Which agency was added to the Second Schedule of the RTI Act in 2011?
x: The CBI was added to the Second Schedule in 2011; the CIC is not exempt as it is the appellate body.

s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 provides for the constitution of State Information Commissions?
x: Section 15 constitutes the State Information Commissions; Section 12 does this for the CIC.

s: Under Section 19(8)(b) of the RTI Act, the Information Commission may require the public authority to:
o: Compensate the applicant for any loss or detriment suffered
Pay a penalty directly to the Information Commissioner
x: Section 19(8)(b) lets the Commission require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.

s: Section 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Imposition of penalty on every delayed applicant
Compulsory adjudication of all RTI appeals by courts
Exemption of personal information from disclosure
Suo motu disclosure by public authorities
x: Section 4 mandates proactive or suo motu disclosure by public authorities, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.

s: Within how many days is a second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission ordinarily filed under the RTI Act?
x: The second appeal lies within ninety days; the first appeal is filed within thirty days.

s: Within what time must information concerning the life or liberty of a person be supplied under the RTI Act?
x: Life or liberty cases must be answered within 48 hours; routing through an APIO gives 35 days and third-party cases 40 days.

s: Within how many days must information sought through an Assistant Public Information Officer be supplied under the RTI Act?
x: An application through an APIO adds 5 days to the normal 30, making 35 days.

s:
Consider the following statements about time limits under the RTI Act:
1. Where third-party information is involved, the reply limit is 40 days.
2. The first appeal must be filed within 90 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: third-party cases (Section 11) take 40 days. Statement 2 is wrong: the first appeal is within 30 days; 90 days is for the second appeal.

s:
Consider the following pairs under the RTI Act, 2005:
1. Normal reply by the PIO - 45 days
2. Information concerning life or liberty - 48 hours
3. First appeal to the First Appellate Authority - within 30 days
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: B is correct (APPSC 2025 key). Pair 1 is wrong: the normal reply period under Section 7 is 30 days, not 45; 45 days applies only to human-rights allegations against Section 24 organisations. Pair 2 is correct: 48 hours. Pair 3 is correct: the first appeal lies within 30 days. A and C include the wrong pair 1; D includes all.

s: Within how many days must information about human-rights allegations against organisations under Section 24 be supplied?
x: Such information must be supplied within 45 days, with the Commission's approval.

s: Within what time must the First Appellate Authority ordinarily decide a first appeal under the RTI Act?
x: A first appeal is filed within 30 days and decided within 30 days, extendable to 45 days.

s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible ground associated with removal of a State Information Commissioner?
o: Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
Disagreement with a decision of the State Government
Proved incapacity after the prescribed inquiry
x: Disagreement with a State Government decision is not a stated ground for removal. Insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude and proved incapacity are recognised grounds.

s: What is the nature of the Central and State Information Commissions?
o: Statutory bodies under the RTI Act
Bodies under the Protection of Human Rights Act
x: Both are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, with civil-court powers, hearing second appeals and complaints.

s: Before the 2019 amendment, to whose salary was the salary of a State Information Commissioner linked?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: A State IC's salary was linked to the Chief Secretary's, while the CIC's equalled the Chief Election Commissioner's.

s: After an inquiry by which body can the Governor remove a State Information Commissioner for proved misbehaviour?
x: Removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity is by the Governor after a Supreme Court inquiry on the Governor's reference.

s: What was the term of an Information Commissioner under the original RTI Act?
o: Three years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 62
Six years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 65
x: The original term was five years or age 65, with no reappointment; since 2019 the Centre notifies it, and the 2019 Rules fix three years.

s: Who chairs the committee that recommends appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The committee is the Chief Minister (chair), the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM; the Governor then appoints.

s: What is the term of office of members of the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: 5 years or until the age of 65
4 years or until the age of 65
3 years or until the age of 65
6 years or until the age of 65
x: The CVC term is 4 years or age 65; 5 years or 65 was the original Information Commission term.

s: Who appoints the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners of the Central Information Commission?
x: Under Section 12, the President appoints them on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, the LoP in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister.

s: What is the term of an Information Commissioner since the RTI Rules 2019?
x: The original term of 5 years or 65 was replaced in 2019 by a term notified by the Centre, 3 years under the RTI Rules 2019.

s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the appointment of the Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
x: The committee has the PM (chair), the LoP in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
A Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The SIC committee has the CM, the LoP in the Assembly and a minister nominated by the CM; the High Court Chief Justice is not on it.

s: Who among the following can NOT be appointed as an Information Commissioner under the RTI Act?
o: A person eminent in social service
x: An Information Commissioner cannot be an MP or MLA; persons eminent in law, journalism or social service are eligible.

s: Who appoints the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Under Section 15 the Governor appoints the State CIC and SICs on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the CM.

s: While inquiring into complaints, the Central and State Information Commissions have the powers of which body?
x: The Information Commissions are statutory bodies with civil-court powers.

s: On whom does the burden of proof lie in penalty proceedings under Section 20 of the RTI Act?
x: The PIO bears the burden of proof and must be heard before a penalty; the Commission may also recommend disciplinary action.

s: What is the penalty that may be imposed on a Public Information Officer under Section 20?
x: Section 20 provides for a penalty of ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000, along with possible disciplinary action.

s: On which of the following grounds can a penalty be imposed on a Public Information Officer under Section 20 of the RTI Act?
o: Knowingly giving incorrect or misleading information
Rejecting a request under Section 8 in good faith
Transferring a request to another public authority
x: Section 20 penalties apply for refusing an application, delay, or knowingly giving incorrect or misleading information.

s:
Consider the following statements about penalties under the RTI Act:
1. The penalty on a PIO is imposed by the Central or State Information Commission.
2. The PIO must be given a hearing before a penalty is imposed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CIC or SIC imposes the penalty under Section 20, and the PIO must be heard first.

s: Besides the Chief Information Commissioner, an Information Commission may have up to how many Information Commissioners?
x: Both the Central and State Information Commissions have a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.

s: Before the 2019 amendment, to whose salary was the salary of the Chief Information Commissioner equal?
x: Originally the CIC's salary equalled the Chief Election Commissioner's and an IC's an Election Commissioner's; since 2019 the Centre fixes it.

s: Who was the Chief Information Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh when the State Information Commission inspected 258 offices in 2026?
x: AP SIC under Chief IC Vajja Srinivasa Rao found Section 4(1)(b) violations in 258 offices in 18 districts.

s: Under Section 8(3) of the RTI Act, after how many years does most exempt information become disclosable?
x: The Section 8(3) rule is 20 years, with exceptions such as cabinet deliberations; Section 8(2) is the public-interest override.

s: How did the Second ARC recommend that the Section 8 exemptions of the RTI Act be interpreted?
x: The Second ARC wanted Section 8 exemptions read narrowly and maximum information placed in the public domain automatically.

s: Under which Section of the RTI Act can a request be rejected because it infringes the copyright of a person other than the State?
x: Section 9 allows rejection on grounds of copyright of a person other than the State; Section 11 deals with third-party information.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Section 8(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Commercial confidence and trade secrets — Section 8(1)(a)
Information held in a fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)
Information from a foreign government in confidence — Section 8(1)(j)
x: Section 8(1)(e) covers information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship. Commercial confidence and trade secrets fall under clause (d), foreign-government information under clause (f), and personal information under clause (j).

s: Under which provision of the RTI Act may exempt information be disclosed if public interest outweighs the harm, even if covered by the Official Secrets Act?
x: Section 8(2) is the public-interest override; 8(3) is the 20-year rule and 8(1)(j) covers personal information.

s: Which of the following pairs (Section 8(1) clause – exempt information) is wrongly matched?
o: 8(1)(f) – Information from a foreign government in confidence
x: Clause 8(1)(i) covers cabinet papers; personal information is 8(1)(j).

s: With which law did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommend that the RTI framework be firmly linked?
x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.

s: Section 44(3) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 altered Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by
o: making personal information a blanket exemption and dropping the earlier public-interest override
transferring all RTI appeals to the Data Protection Board
requiring every applicant to disclose the reason for seeking personal information
removing all exemptions relating to personal information
x: Section 44(3) rewrote Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, dropping the earlier test concerning relationship to public activity, unwarranted invasion of privacy and the public-interest override.

s:
Consider the following statements about amendments to the RTI Act:
1. The 2019 amendment changed the tenure and salaries of Information Commissioners.
2. Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act, 2023 altered Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: 2019 changed tenure and pay; DPDP 2023 Section 44(3) rewrote 8(1)(j) into a blanket exemption for personal information.

s: The Second ARC recommended linking the RTI regime with which law to protect RTI activists?
x: With over 100 RTI activists killed, the Second ARC urged linking RTI with whistle-blower protection; the 2014 Act is not operationalised.

s: When did the Supreme Court refer the challenge to the DPDP amendment of the RTI Act to a Constitution Bench?
x: The amendment was notified in November 2025 and the challenge was referred to a Constitution Bench in February 2026; on 7 August 2026 the Court agreed to examine repugnancy.

s: The principal criticism of the 2019 changes relating to the tenure and salaries of Information Commissions is that they
o: removed the power of the Commissions to impose penalties
weakened the autonomy of the Commissions by placing tenure and pay in executive hands
made all decisions of the Commissions subject to approval by political parties
x: The criticism is that executive control over tenure and remuneration may weaken the institutional autonomy of the Information Commissions.

s: The CIC has ruled that which of the following is NOT a public authority under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act?
o: Office of the Chief Justice of India
An NGO substantially financed by Government
x: The CIC ruled that the BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h); the CJI's office and substantially financed NGOs are.

s: The demand to bring political parties under the RTI Act is intended to:
o: Check corruption and crony capitalism and scrutinise illegal foreign contributions
x: Activists cite checking corruption and crony capitalism, scrutiny of illegal foreign contributions and parties' state privileges such as free Doordarshan airtime.

s: In June 2013, how many national political parties did the Central Information Commission declare public authorities under the RTI Act?
x: The CIC declared six national parties - INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP - public authorities; the Aam Aadmi Party was not among them.

s: What happened to the RTI (Amendment) Bill, 2013, which sought to exclude political parties from the RTI Act?
o: Was struck down by the Supreme Court
Was referred to the Law Commission
x: Parties did not comply with the CIC's 2013 order, and the 2013 Bill to exclude them lapsed; the matter is pending before the Supreme Court.

s: On which portal are MPLADS works, which are covered under the RTI Act, tracked?
x: MPLADS works are covered by RTI and tracked on the eSAKSHI portal.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold in 2019 that NGOs substantially financed by government are public authorities under the RTI Act?
x: In the DAV College Trust case (2019) substantially financed NGOs were held to be public authorities.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold evaluated answer sheets to be in CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)?
o: Held in a fiduciary capacity and hence exempt
Accessible only through a court order
x: Evaluated answer sheets are information that examinees can inspect, and the examining body does not hold them in a fiduciary capacity.

s: In the Zee Telefilms case, the Supreme Court held that the BCCI:
o: Performs public functions but is not 'State' under Article 12
Is 'State' and a public authority under the RTI Act
x: Zee Telefilms held that BCCI performs public functions but is not State under Article 12; a later CIC ruling held it is not a public authority under Section 2(h).

s: Which of the following pairs (RTI-related case – decision) is wrongly matched?
o: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay – Evaluated answer sheets are information accessible to examinees
CPIO, Supreme Court v. Subhash Chandra Agarwal – Office of the CJI is a public authority under the RTI Act
Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. CIC – Service records and tax returns of a public servant are personal information
Zee Telefilms v. Union of India – Office of the CJI is a public authority under the RTI Act
x: Zee Telefilms held that the BCCI is not 'State' under Article 12; the CJI's office ruling came in Subhash Chandra Agarwal.

s: What did Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v CIC (2012) hold the service records, assets and tax returns of an employee to be?
o: Information that must be proactively disclosed
x: The Supreme Court held these to be personal information under Section 8(1)(j).

s: Which case held the office of the Chief Justice of India to be a public authority under the RTI Act?
o: Namit Sharma v Union of India
Zee Telefilms v Union of India
CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal
x: A Constitution Bench in CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019) held the CJI's office to be a public authority.

s: What happened to the 2014 Madras High Court remark that an RTI applicant should state reasons for seeking information?
o: It was upheld by the Supreme Court
It was adopted by the CIC as a rule
x: The remark was withdrawn because Section 6(2) says no reason need be given.

s: Which body runs the RTI Online portal for central public authorities, launched in 2013?
x: The RTI Online portal (rtionline.gov.in) of the DoPT was launched in 2013 for applications, first appeals and online fees.

s: What did the Andhra Pradesh High Court direct the State to set up in November 2023?
x: Following the Supreme Court's Pravasi Legal Cell judgment, the AP High Court directed the state to set up an online RTI portal.

s: When was the new website of the Andhra Pradesh State Information Commission (sic.ap.gov.in) launched?
x: The AP SIC launched its new website sic.ap.gov.in on 8 September 2025.

s: What is a major institutional reason for delays in disposal of RTI matters?
o: Chronic vacancies in the Central and State Information Commissions
x: Chronic vacancies in the CIC and State Information Commissions, together with a large backlog of appeals, cause long delays.

s: Which of the following is NOT a criticism of the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
x: Appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists are the identified concerns; excessive speed in disposal is not a criticism.

s: What was the approximate number of RTI appeals and complaints pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026?
x: More than 4 lakh RTI appeals and complaints were reported to be pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026.

s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggested re-examination of the RTI framework mainly in the context of exempting which of the following categories of information?
o: Only information supplied by private bodies
All information held by local authorities
All records relating to public expenditure and contracts
Confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
x: The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.

s: More than how many RTI activists were reported to have been killed by July 2026?
x: Reports cited that more than 100 RTI activists had been killed by July 2026.

s: Which organisation released a 2025 report card finding significant gaps as the RTI Act turned 20?
x: The Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025 report card found significant gaps in the functioning of the Act.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the All India Services?
x: Article 312 concerns All India Services; 309 covers recruitment, 311 safeguards and 320 PSC functions.

s: A member of a Public Service Commission is proposed to be removed for misbehaviour. Which procedure is constitutionally relevant?
o: Removal by the Chief Minister after consultation with the State Cabinet
An inquiry by the Supreme Court before removal for misbehaviour
Removal by the Governor without any inquiry
Removal by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha after a simple majority vote
x: B is correct: a member of a Public Service Commission can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court. A, C and D are wrong because neither the Chief Minister, nor the Governor without inquiry, nor the Lok Sabha Speaker by a vote can remove a PSC member.

s: What is the term of office of a member of the Union Public Service Commission?
o: 5 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
4 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
x: C is correct: a UPSC member serves 6 years or until 65. B is the limit for State and Joint PSC members (6 years or 62). A was the original Information Commissioner term; D is the CVC term.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides safeguards such as inquiry and hearing before dismissal of a civil servant?
x: Article 311 gives safeguards; Article 310 is the doctrine of pleasure and 312 the All India Services.

s: A member of a State Public Service Commission holds office for 6 years or until what age?
x: SPSC/JSPSC members serve 6 years or until 62; UPSC members until 65.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions?
x: Article 320 lays down the functions of PSCs; 315 sets them up, 316 covers appointment and term, 317 removal.

s: Under Article 312, which House of Parliament can start the creation of a new All India Service by passing a resolution?
o: Either House by a simple majority
A joint sitting of both Houses
x: Article 312 lets Parliament create a new All India Service after a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by two-thirds of members present and voting.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union or a State?
x: Article 309 deals with recruitment and conditions of service; 310 is the doctrine of pleasure.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission?
x: Article 315 sets up PSCs, 316 covers appointment and term, and 317 covers removal and suspension.

s: Which body's recommendations are associated with a code of ethics, the Right to Public Services and e-governance?
x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) is linked with a code of ethics, the Right to Public Services and e-governance. Shanta Kumar dealt with FCI/PDS, Ashok Dalwai with farmers' income and Kasturirangan with education.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to committees on the Civil Services Examination is wrongly matched?
o: D.S. Kothari Committee – Introduction of the three-stage examination system
Y.K. Alagh Committee – Introduction of the three-stage examination system
Satish Chandra Committee – Review of the Kothari scheme and introduction of an essay paper
P.C. Hota Committee – Civil service reforms
x: The Y.K. Alagh Committee reviewed the CSE system; the three-stage examination came from the D.S. Kothari Committee.

s: Which issues did the B.S. Baswan Committee, constituted in 2016, examine?
o: The introduction of the essay paper alone
Age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern
The three-stage examination system introduced in 1979
x: The B.S. Baswan Committee examined the age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern for the Civil Services Examination.

s: Who headed the committee set up by the UPSC in July 2000 to review the Civil Services Examination scheme?
x: Standard sources identify the July 2000 committee set up by the UPSC with Y.K. Alagh. Sukhadeo Thorat is named in a conflicting examination key, but the standard identification is Alagh.

s: Which committee (1976) recommended the three-stage Civil Services Examination of Prelims, Mains and Interview?
x: The D.S. Kothari Committee (1976) gave the three-stage CSE adopted from 1979.

s: Which of the following pairs (committee – year) is correctly matched?
x: The P.C. Hota Committee was formed in February 2004; Kothari was 1976, Satish Chandra 1989 and Baswan 2016.

s: What was the title of the Fourth Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
x: The 4th Report was 'Ethics in Governance'; 'Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights' was the 10th Report.

s: Who chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission constituted in 2005?
x: M. Veerappa Moily chaired the 2nd ARC (31 August 2005), which gave 15 reports, the first on RTI as the 'Master Key to Good Governance'.

s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level
Abolition of right to public services laws
x: The Commission recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition. It also supported lateral entry, performance-based appraisal and rotational postings.

s: What was the title of the 12th Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights
Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
x: The 12th Report was 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance'; the 4th was Ethics and the 10th Personnel Administration.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It was constituted in 2005.
2. Its first report dealt with Right to Information.
3. It recommended abolition of right to public services laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (constituted 31 Aug 2005; 1st Report on RTI). Statement 3 is wrong: it recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition.

s: How many reports did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission submit?
x: The Second ARC, constituted on 31 August 2005, submitted 15 reports between June 2006 and May 2009.

s: What was the title of the 10th Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
x: The 10th Report dealt with personnel administration: 'Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights'.

s: Which report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with personnel administration?
x: The 10th Report was on personnel administration; the 4th was on ethics and the 12th on citizen-centric administration.

s: Who succeeded M. Veerappa Moily as chairman of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
x: The Second ARC (31 Aug 2005) was chaired by M. Veerappa Moily and later by V. Ramachandran.

s: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry into the civil services at which level?
x: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level, along with performance-based appraisal.

s: Civil Services Day is observed on 21 April because on 21 April 1947:
o: The Federal Public Service Commission was renamed UPSC
Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi
The first All India Service was created
The UPSC was established in New Delhi
x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”

s: Where did Sardar Patel address the first probationers on 21 April 1947, calling them the 'steel frame of India'?
x: Patel's address was at Metcalfe House, Delhi; the first Civil Services Day function was held at Vigyan Bhawan in 2006.

s: Which day is observed in India on 21 April every year?
x: Civil Services Day (21 April) marks Sardar Patel's 1947 address to the first probationers.

s:
Consider the following statements about Civil Services Day:
1. It marks Sardar Patel's address to the first probationers at Metcalfe House in 1947.
2. The first Civil Services Day function was held at Vigyan Bhawan in 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Patel spoke on 21 April 1947 and the first function was at Vigyan Bhawan on 21 April 2006.

s: What does the split system in civil administration separate?
o: Policy formulation in the Secretariat from implementation through field agencies
x: The split system separates policy functions performed by the Secretariat from implementation carried out by field agencies.

s: What does the tenure system under the Central Staffing Scheme refer to?
o: Permanent transfer of every State officer to the Union Government
A fixed term of service at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre
Rotation only among district offices within a State
Appointment of Central officers exclusively to local governments
x: Under the tenure system, State-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre and then return to their State cadre.

s: Which is the cadre-controlling authority for the Indian Police Service?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: MHA controls the IPS cadre; DoPT controls the IAS and MoEFCC the Indian Forest Service.

s:
Civil servants perform which of the following roles in public administration?
1. Policy advisers
2. Implementers of public policy
3. Stabilisers of the administrative system
x: Civil servants serve as policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers in public administration; therefore, all three statements are correct.

s: Which is the cadre-controlling authority for the IAS?
x: The IAS cadre is controlled by the DoPT, the IPS by the MHA and the Indian Forest Service by the MoEFCC.

s: Which ministry is the cadre-controlling authority for the Indian Forest Service?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The MoEFCC controls the Indian Forest Service cadre.

s: Max Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy is based on which type of authority?
x: Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy rests on legal-rational authority, with hierarchy, rules, impersonality, merit and written files, not personal patronage.

s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the types of bureaucracy identified by F. Morstein Marx?
x: F. Morstein Marx identified guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies in The Administrative State.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of bureaucracy given by F. Morstein Marx?
x: Morstein Marx (The Administrative State) gave guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies; 'rational' is not one of them.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Max Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy?
x: Weber's legal-rational bureaucracy rests on hierarchy, rules, impersonality and merit, not personal patronage.

s: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards to insulate civil servants from political pressure were recommended in which case?
x: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards are associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian case and the Second ARC.

s: Which rules require political neutrality and integrity from the concerned civil servants?
o: Civil Services Examination Rules, 1968 and Election Rules, 1964
All India Services Act, 1935 and CCS Rules, 1947
x: The AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 require political neutrality and integrity.

s: In which year were the CCS (Conduct) Rules, which require political neutrality of central government employees, framed?
x: The CCS (Conduct) Rules 1964 and the AIS (Conduct) Rules 1968 require political neutrality and integrity.

s: Who among the following supported lateral entry into the civil services?
o: Neither the Second ARC nor the Hota Committee
Both the Second ARC and the Hota Committee
x: Both the Second ARC and the P.C. Hota Committee supported lateral entry; a UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.

s: Who is the custodian of Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building?
x: Mission Karmayogi (2020) runs on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and its custodian is the Capacity Building Commission, not the UPSC.

s: Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, runs on which online platform?
x: Mission Karmayogi (2020) runs on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, with the Capacity Building Commission as custodian.

s: In which year was Mission Karmayogi launched?
x: Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, began in 2020.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six pillars of Mission Karmayogi?
x: Karmayogi's six pillars are policy, institutional, competency, digital learning (iGOT), e-HRMS and monitoring-evaluation frameworks.

s: When did the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 come into force?
x: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act came into force on 1 July 2005.

s: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, who can attach 'proceeds of crime'?
x: The ED Director can attach proceeds of crime under the PMLA.

s: Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, when may the Special Court confiscate a fugitive's property on the ED's application?
o: Only after a Supreme Court order
x: On the ED's application, the Special Court may confiscate property even before conviction.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 — Proceedings involving flight from India and confiscation by a Special Court
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 — Attachment and confiscation of proceeds of corruption
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Ban on proxy holdings
Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 — Imprisonment up to ten years as its stated maximum punishment
x: The Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 provides for confiscation and imprisonment up to seven years, not ten years. The other pairings are correctly stated.

s: Under the Benami Transactions (Amendment) Act, 2016, up to how many years of rigorous imprisonment is benami holding punishable?
x: The Benami Act provides confiscation and up to 7 years' rigorous imprisonment, not ten.

s: What is the minimum value of the offence for the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 to apply?
x: The FEOA applies where there is a warrant, an offence of ₹100 crore or more, and flight from India.

s: In which year did India ratify the United Nations Convention against Corruption?
x: The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005 and ratified it in 2011.

s: In which year did India sign the UN Convention against Corruption?
x: UNCAC was adopted in 2003, signed by India in 2005 and ratified in 2011.

s: Who publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
x: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, headquartered in Berlin.

s: On the Corruption Perceptions Index scale of 0 to 100, what does a score of 0 denote?
x: The CPI measures perceived public-sector corruption on a 0-100 scale, where 0 denotes highly corrupt conditions.

s: What was India's rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025?
x: In CPI 2025 India ranked 91st of 182 with a score of 39; in 2024 it was 96th with 38.

s: What does the Corruption Perceptions Index measure?
x: The CPI of Transparency International measures perceived public-sector corruption from expert and business surveys.

s: Where is Transparency International, which publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index, headquartered?
x: Transparency International is based in Berlin and has published the CPI every year since 1995.

s: Since which year has Transparency International published the Corruption Perceptions Index?
x: Transparency International (Berlin) has published the CPI every year since 1995.

s: What was India's score in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025?
x: In CPI 2025 India scored 39 and ranked 91st of 182 (38 and 96th in 2024).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act?
o: Bribe-giving became a direct offence punishable with up to seven years
It sought to align Indian law with the UN Convention against Corruption
Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf
A coerced bribe-giver is protected only if the matter is reported within 30 days
x: A coerced bribe-giver must report within 7 days, not 30.

s: Under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act, what imprisonment does a public servant convicted of taking a bribe face?
x: The amended Act prescribes three to seven years' imprisonment and a fine; trials should end within two years, extendable to four.

s: Under Section 2(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which of the following does NOT correctly describe a 'public servant'?
o: An employee of a local authority
Only a permanent employee of the Union Government
A person whose office requires performance of a public duty
x: The definition covers local-authority employees, Judges and persons performing public duties; it is not limited to permanent Union employees.

s: Under the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act, within what time must a coerced bribe-giver report the matter to be protected?
x: A coerced bribe-giver is protected if he reports within 7 days, not 30.

s: Under the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018, trial must be completed within 2 years; up to what maximum period can it be extended?
x: The trial must finish within 2 years, extendable to a maximum of 4 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. Bribe-giving was made a direct offence punishable with up to 7 years.
2. Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf.
3. Its purpose was to align the law with UNCAC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: bribe-giving became a direct offence (up to 7 years), commercial organisations became liable, and the aim was alignment with UNCAC.

s: In the split verdict on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, who struck it down as violating Article 14?
x: Justice Nagarathna struck Section 17A down under Article 14; Justice Viswanathan upheld it subject to a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion.

s: Which section of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires prior sanction before a court takes cognizance of an offence?
x: Section 19 requires prior sanction before cognizance; Section 17A requires government approval before inquiry or investigation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanction for prosecution of public servants?
o: Section 19 of the PC Act requires government approval before a police inquiry begins
Section 218 of the BNSS, corresponding to Section 197 CrPC, came into force on 1 July 2024
Since 2018, Section 19 sanction under the PC Act also covers retired public servants
Approval before an inquiry or investigation is governed by Section 17A of the PC Act
x: Prior approval before inquiry or investigation is Section 17A; Section 19 concerns sanction for prosecution.

s: Which Supreme Court judgments are cited as earlier precedents that struck down prior-sanction requirements for investigating public servants?
x: Vineet Narain (1997) and Subramanian Swamy (2014) struck down prior-sanction rules, the backdrop to the Section 17A challenge. Kesavananda and Minerva Mills concern the basic structure; Prakash Singh is police reform and Vishaka sexual harassment at the workplace; Lalita Kumari (mandatory FIR) and Arnesh Kumar (arrest guidelines) are not about prior sanction.

s: Which of the following pairs (provision – stage of protection) is correctly matched?
o: Sec 218 BNSS – General protection of public servants
x: Sec 218 BNSS (earlier Sec 197 CrPC) is the general protection; 17A is approval before investigation and 19 sanction before cognizance.

s: Before which of the following does Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act require government approval?
o: Inquiry or investigation into official decisions
Arrest of a retired public servant
x: Section 17A requires approval before inquiry or investigation; Section 19 requires sanction before a court takes cognizance.

s: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in which year?
x: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in 2014. The reference to 2011 relates to the year in which the Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha.
